text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National carrier Nigeria Airways planes banned by British Civil Aviation Authority from flying to Britain until the airline produces certificate of insurance.

- International Narcotics Control Board hails Nigeria's efforts at fighting illicit drugs and says Nigeria, Egypt, Burkina Faso and Namibia are the only four African nations that have complied with conventions of the board.

- Sixteen African countries have indicated their intention to participate in 7th All African trade and tourism fair due to open in northern city of Kaduna on March 29, says chairman of organising committee Salisu Ahmed.
- Electoral commission begins nationwide screening of candidates for local council polls scheduled for March 15 and says it will allow appeals by those disqualified.

- British firm TAD Eurotube Ltd was last December awarded a 1.25 billion naira contract to supply alloy, carbon and stainless tubes to Nigerian liquefied natural gas project, it emerged at a seminar on Tuesday by a visiting British trade mission.
- Tribunal gives bail to eight university lecturers facing sedition and arson charges in eastern Enugu city.
- Dunlop Nigeria may have sacked executives of the workers' union following last week's disturbances which led to brief closure of the company.
- British high commissioner (ambassador) to Nigeria, Thorold Masefield, says privatisation benefited his country's oil and gas industry tremendously and commends same to Nigeria.
